suggestions.title: Readiness never checks that compare and checks were read at pr.headSha, yet it returns pr.headSha as the head that is ready
suggestions.failurePath: `pr.headSha` is used only in the return value (line 399). Nothing ties `compare` or `checks` to that head. Probe at head: green inputs with `compare.commits = [EARLIER]`, which does not contain `pr.headSha`, and the body link moved to EARLIER. The result is ready=true and headSha=HEAD. Suppose a future S4 shell reads compare or checks at an older head than the PR it reads (a cached webhook payload, a compare by branch name across a push). The digest D and the verdicts at D then describe the older patch, and readiness reports the newer, unreviewed head as ready. S5 and P4 would then stamp success on that head and merge it.
suggestions.evidence: GateInputs.compare (line 91) and checks (lines 78-83) carry no head SHA. Lines 272-276 compute the digest from compare.files without any head check. Line 399 returns `headSha: pr?.headSha`. A cheap guard inside the pure function: block (as patch-unavailable or pr-unreadable) unless `compare.commits` contains `pr.headSha` (with commits read in full, as the contract says, the head is in base..head). Alternatively, add `headSha` to the compare and checks inputs and require it to equal pr.headSha.

suggestions.title: verify-missing detail says verdicts are on another patch even when they are on the current one
suggestions.failurePath: Take a single verify verdict at the current digest D with outcome `step_failed` (or `tampered` or `unbound`). Readiness emits verify-missing with detail "1 verdict(s) on another patch or unbound". The verdict is on this patch; the verify step failed. The status description and the chief tool would send a person looking for a patch mismatch that does not exist. Probe output at head: `["verify-missing","transient","1 verdict(s) on another patch or unbound"]`.
suggestions.evidence: Line 356 counts `i.verdicts.filter((x) => x.kind === 'verify').length`, which is every verify verdict of the build, including the ones in `verify` at D whose outcomes are not in the counted list. Counting only verdicts with `x.patchDigest !== D`, and naming step_failed separately, would make the detail accurate. The test at merge-gate-readiness.test.ts:511-515 checks only the code.

suggestions.title: Check runs deduplicated by name alone, combined with the unstable exemption for the gate's own status, can hide a failing check
suggestions.failurePath: The contract asks the shell for only the latest run per name (line 43). Suppose two different check suites (another workflow or app) report a run with the same name on the head, the older one failing and the newer passing. The shell keeps only the passing one, while GitHub's rollup can still count the failing one and report `unstable`. The gate's own status is pending or failure until it first says ready, so `ownNotPassing` is true and `notPassing` is empty. Lines 250-254 then add no mergeable-state blocker, and readiness can go ready while GitHub shows a failing check. This depends on how the S4 shell dedupes, and on GitHub counting same-named runs from different suites separately. This repo's ci.yml limits push runs to main, so it is a contract risk rather than one seen today.
suggestions.evidence: Line 43: `外壳只传每个名字最新的一条`. Lines 244-254: in the `unstable` branch, `else if (!ownNotPassing)` is the only guard when no foreign non-passing check is visible. Keying the dedupe by (app or suite, name) in the input contract, or skipping the own-status exemption while the gate's status is not yet success, would close it.

suggestions.title: Blocking verdicts on an earlier digest are never tested as not counting: the review, verify and chief block checks can be made sticky across digests without any test failing
suggestions.evidence: Test 466 moves only the baseline verdicts, which are all passes, to 'pd1:old'. No test puts a review, verify or decision 'block' on an earlier digest next to passes on D. In a scratch copy of the head, three mutations each left 114 of 114 passing. Mutation 1, at readiness.ts:363: `at('review').filter(...)` changed to `i.verdicts.filter((x) => x.kind === 'review' && x.outcome === 'block')`. Mutation 2, at readiness.ts:347: verify-failed read from all verdicts. Mutation 3, at readiness.ts:374: decision-no-go read from all verdicts. None of these mutations is in s2-mutations-*.txt. The closest one, 'verdicts on any digest count', removes the digest filter everywhere and is caught only through the pass side.
suggestions.failurePath: The code at the head is correct: at() filters by D. The gap is in the tests. The PR claims that verdicts count only at the current patch digest, and the ticket says a code change voids the old verdict (failure mode 5), and that applies to blocks too. A regression could make a block on an earlier digest still count. Then after a [review-fix] round produces patch D2, with every perspective, verify and chief passing at D2, the D1 block would keep review-blocking, verify-failed or decision-no-go set for the rest of the build. The fix round could never reach ready, and no readiness test would turn red. A fix: add a test with a block at 'pd1:old' plus passes at D that expects [], one per kind.

suggestions.title: A null patchDigest is never tested on its own: the 'unbound' test also flips the outcome, so a {pass, null} verdict counting, or a {tampered, null} one being ignored, both pass the suite
suggestions.evidence: Test 472, '未绑定 head 的判定（patchDigest 为空）不算', sets patchDigest: null and outcome: 'unbound' together. 'unbound' is not in the list of counted outcomes at readiness.ts:353, so the test passes whatever the digest filter does. GateVerdictView documents a null patchDigest as the head-mismatch marker (readiness.ts:24-25) and allows any outcome with it. Both tampered verdicts in the tests use 'pd1:old' (lines 347 and 570). In a scratch copy of the head, two mutations each left 114 of 114 passing. Mutation 1, at readiness.ts:340: `x.patchDigest === D` changed to `(x.patchDigest === D || x.patchDigest === null)`. Mutation 2, at readiness.ts:332: tampered counted only when `x.patchDigest !== null`.
suggestions.failurePath: Failure modes 1 and 6 depend on this. A verify pass whose head is not the expected head arrives as {kind: 'verify', outcome: 'pass', patchDigest: null}, a verdict recorded after a push. If the filter regresses so null counts as current, verify-missing goes away and readiness can be true for a patch nobody verified. Separately, a verifier that commits outside docs/verify/ moves the head, so its tampered verdict can be unbound too ({tampered, null}). If the tamper check regresses to bound verdicts only, verify-tampered goes away. Neither regression turns a test red. A fix: add a {pass, null} test expecting verify-missing, and a {tampered, null} row expecting verify-tampered.

suggestions.failurePath: The PR's Risk section calls the vocabulary a contract for S5 to S9, and per merge-gate.ts:163-164 the class decides whether the gate waits or fix-rounds ('transient') or stops for a person ('human'). Ticket failure modes 3 (timeout gives no go) and 6 (tamper) rely on those codes being 'human'. A later edit that makes them 'transient' would let S7 keep redispatching or fix-rounding a tampered lane or a timed-out perspective, and no readiness test would catch it. A fix: a single table test that asserts code → class for all 50 codes.
